quests.title: Echoes of an Unfinished Past

dialogue.t: Oh! It's {NICKNAME} and Paimon! Nice to see you again!
Um... Miss Priestess, have we met somewhere before? You don't seem that familiar to Paimon...
Hey! It's me! Seriously, we met not long ago... Can't you recognize me by my voice?
Oh yeah, it's you! You're the one from back when— Uhh... Wait, who are you exactly? This is starting to sound like some kinda weird scam...

Aww, my adorable little Paimon didn't even recognize me... That really stings. But I'll let it slide — after all, you did call me "Miss Priestess." I guess it's fair, since I never took off my helmet back at Thunderclap Reef...
Wait, hang on! Don't tell Paimon... you're Verna!? You're really, actually a priestess from the Frostmoon Scions!?
E—Excuse you! That's a weird way to say hello! Seriously, you won't find a priestess more reliable than me anywhere else! There was never any reason to doubt me in the first place!
Ahem! Anyway, this must be the Moon Mai{RUBY#[D]Kuutar}den's guidance at work — how else could I be so fortunate as to run into you both at a time like this?

dialogue.sit: Well, we were just passing through...
I have a bad feeling about this...

dialogue.t: Exactly! That's what we call fate. "With her silver spindle, she weaves paths as one, whether they be of the rich, or the—" Uh, or the...
Anyway, let's forget about all that. {NICKNAME}, Paimon, you remember what that imposter said before, right?
You mean that priestess-looking lady who seemed more legit than you? She said she'd be waiting at the Court of the First Edict... or something like that?
Ahem... That "more legit than you" bit was totally uncalled for. But since you've got such a good memory, Paimon, and since you're both going to help me out later, I'll let it slide!
Hey! Paimon hasn't agreed to help you out yet! Why is it that every time we talk to you, we end up second-guessing reality...?
Uh, don't sweat the details! More importantly, I've already come up with a flawless, super-ultra reliable plan. We'll catch that imposter in no time!
Think about it. She said she'd be waiting in the sealed-off sanctum no one can even get into, right? So obviously...
She wants us to get curious and break the seal, letting her sneak in and snatch whatever treasure's inside!
And my super-foolproof plan is to turn the tables on her! Once we open the gates of the sanctum, she'll definitely show up, and that's when we'll catch her!
Pretty solid plan, right? I'd say it'd hold up just fine against those top-notch detectives from Papa Wrench's books!
Seriously?! That sounds even crazier than the plan you had at Thunderclap Reef! You just told us no one's been able to unseal the Court of the First Edict for centuries!
Only because they didn't have me, along with the super reliable tag-team combination that is the two of you!
After we parted ways, I've been thinking... Since the Court of the First Edict was sealed by kuuvahki, maybe we can disrupt it the same way we did at Thunderclap Reef...
And so— Ta-dah! See? I had my little Krakas look for more of those special fragments, and I pieced them all together!
And the moment I managed to distract Eveliina, bam! You two showed up! Tell me we're not fated to reunite!
Fated? More like fatal! Are you sure this won't mess up the weather on Hiisi Island like it did back at Thunderclap Reef?
No worries! This time, I'll be in full control of the kuuvahki. And besides, everything turned out just fine back at the Reef, didn't it?
Now then! {NICKNAME}, Paimon, prepare to witness the miracle of science!
W—Wait! If someone's gotta throw it, let us do it! If we leave it to you, this already sketchy plan's bound to get even sketchier...
Come on, I told you there's nothing to worry about! See? This is the power of science!
Hurray! The power of scien— Hey, wait a second! You almost had Paimon fooled! This has nothing to do with science! It was just {NICKNAME} tossing the fragments up there!
Well, since the super reliable {NICKNAME} is also someone who believes in science, I guess that explanation works too.
Alright! "Since the Moon Ma{RUBY#[D]Kuutar}iden has spun a silvery path for us, what awaits beyond the threshold must be..." Umm... wait, how did the rest of it go again...?
Ahem, anyway... since the Moonlane has appeared, it means our plan is working fine. All we need to do is follow it. This is the guidance of the Moon Goddess... Yep!
A—Are you sure? Paimon thinks there's a good chance this path doesn't lead to our destination, but rather somewhere higher up...
Come on, Paimon, come on! You've got a super reliable priestess and a super reliable adventurer on your side — what's there to worry about?
We'd better get moving, before the other priestesses show up— Ahem, I mean, while the Moon Goddess is still showing us the way! Onward and upward!
Umm... Verna, where are we? This doesn't really look like a sanctum...
Yeah, it really doesn't... Ahem! I mean, that's not important! Don't worry! This place has things that resemble Moonlanes, so that means the Moon Maiden is still guiding us... p—probably!
Let us follow the path illuminated by the moonlight, and leave the rest to the will of the moon.
That actually sounded pretty priestess-y coming from you, Verna... Wait, no! Isn't that just a fancy way of saying "I don't know what to do, let's just leave it to fate"?!
Hey! What do you mean "pretty priestess-y"? Have you ever met a priestess who's anything less than super priestess-y?
You've gotta have as much faith in the Moon Maiden's guidance as you do in the power of science! Besides, it's not like we've found any other way down...
Hehe, just like I predicted! See? As long as we follow the guidance of the Moon Goddess, everything'll fall right into place!
Well, if you say so... But are we really sure it's a good idea to open up a place that's been sealed for centuries?
Oh, it'll be totally fine! You've got the most trustworthy priestess of the Frostmoon Scions right here, there's absolutely nothing to worry abou—
Krodo! Did you see where those suspicious intruders were headed?
They took off toward the Court of the First Edict. Not many places to hide around here, after all.
Hmph. You two, check on the seal. I'll inform the Lady Moonchanter. Let's see them try getting away...

Causing trouble in the sacred lands of the Frost Moon... They've got a death wish! The only way they're getting out of this in one piece is if they're somehow the Lady Kuu{RUBY#[D]Moon Maiden}tar herself...
Uhh... Verna? Still wanna tell us "there's absolutely nothing to worry about"?

I... Uhh... Ahaha! Yep! That's right! There's absolutely nothing to worry about! Now that the seal's been opened, all we have to do is set a trap and wait for that imposter to walk right into our hands...
...I'm sorry, I'm so sorry! There's absolutely everything to worry about! I should never have messed with the seal... What do we do now?! Help me, {NICKNAME}, please! *sobs*...

dialogue.sit: Yelling for help like a crybaby doesn't mean someone's magically going to save your butt!
No turning back now. Let's see what's inside.

dialogue.t: Exactly! Well, since the seal's already broken, we might as well head in and take a look... But Verna, you'd better remember to say sorry to everyone in the Frostmoon Scions when we're done here!
Hmm, something about this place feels off compared to what Paimon imagined a sanctum would be... It doesn't feel all that sacred. Smells kinda funny instead...
Haha, well, it has been sealed for 500 years, y'know? Scientifically speaking, rusted metal giving off a blood-like smell isn't too surprising.
By the way, the hymns say that before Lady Aila sealed it, this was where all the Frostmoon followers held their ceremonies! So it's super sacred, really!
Calling it "super sacred" just makes it sound less sacred by the minute!
Oh, come on, don't get hung up on the wording! Look over there — that's the Verdant Crest! Legend says it's the sacred tree that witnessed the birth of the Moon Mai{RUBY#[D]Kuutar}den!
And that pool over there... Uh, if I'm guessing right, that should be the ever-flowing White S{RUBY#[D]Vellamo}pring, blessed by Lady Aila herself!
Do you really have to guess? Also, are you sure you didn't just make those names up?
Hey! I might be a fairly reliable priestess, but even I've never seen these sacred relics from five hundred years ago with my own eyes!
Nor did I ever think I'd get to see something this historically significant... I'm so lucky. All thanks to you, {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

dialogue.sit: Let's stay here for a bit.
Just remember to apologize to everyone after we get out.

dialogue.t: Yes, yes, no problem! I'll do whatever you say, {NICKNAME}!
Just standing in place does feel like a waste, though... Since we're here, why not take a quick walk around?
Hmm? There's something beneath the water. Is that a sword?
Huh? Why would there be a sword here? ...Wait. Hold on. Could this be the ritual sword forged from Hyperborean moonlight that Lady Aila supposedly left behind...!?
The blade that was used to offer up the very first drop of blood under the new moon... Whoa!
I—It's a kuuhenki... Hmm, does it want us to follow it?
Ah, you're here. Wait, that will get the altar dirty...
Eek! When the heck did you get in here? We were the ones who opened the seal first... right?

dialogue.sit: Something's off...
Good thing the treasure chests are still here.

dialogue.t: You're right... But this isn't just "off." It looks like this is a residual image left behind by the Moon Goddes{RUBY#[D]kuuvahki}s's blessing...
And it's been left inside the Court of the First Edict... Maybe this... might be the first Moonchanter herself, Lady Aila...

dialogue.sit: Is that really possible?
Doesn't sound very... Umm... scientific.

dialogue.t: S—Scientifically speaking, it's impossible — but if this is truly Lady Aila, then it wouldn't be surprising for her power to be unscientifically potent...
Oh my days... I can't believe I kept calling THE Lady Aila an imposter... Thank the Moon Goddess she can't hear me anymore...

dialogue.sit: And that explains why her words were always so hard to understand...
And that explains why she seemed like a more legit priestess than you...

dialogue.t: There, that should do it.

dialogue.sit: (This power... is the Lady Aila before us really just a lingering image?)

dialogue.t: ...What did you do, Miss Aila?
Aaahh! W—Where did that voice just come from?!
Hmm... Maybe it got recorded along with the first Moonchanter's image? I mean, even the Moon Goddes{RUBY#[D]kuuvahki}s's blessing couldn't be precise enough to capture just one person's voice, right?
Hehe... There's no need to be so tense. That woman who shares my bloodline surely showed you a few of these low-brow tricks before, hmm?
This is merely a blessing that records awareness, so that <color=#00E1FFFF>the brave warrior over there</color> can hear our words.
P—Paimon's not dreaming, is she? Paimon swears she just looked right at us!
Come on, Paimon, you're most definitely dreaming. What we're seeing now was recorded five hundred years ago, there's no way she could actually see us...
"Over there"? But I don't see anyone...

Ah, never mind. I probably wouldn't understand even if you explained it to me. And whatever tangled past lies between you and her... I'm in no position to judge. Regardless, thank you for your help, Miss Aila.

Lovia should have known better. The wounds left in the wake of the atrocities that old witch inflicted upon you both run deep — of course, the scars fester with resentment. What surprises me is that she trusted you so deeply.
Uh, Verna, who's this Lovia they mentioned? Paimon feels like she's heard that name before...

She was the leader of Frostmoon Scions five hundred years ago, but she was stricken from memory for the sin of blasphemy. Normally, only senior — and super reliable — priestesses like me would even know about her...
Uh, if even someone like you knows about her, then it can't be that much of a secret, can it...?
Hey! Rude! What do you mean, "someone like me"? But seriously, her identity should be top secret. Ordinary followers and folks from the outside aren't supposed to have even heard that name.
Resentment? For what? Everything you and I went through was always meant to be. There is no past or future — because the past is the future.
Your gaze is upon me now, but all you can see is this one fleeting moment. Thanks to Lovia's blessing — the blessing of our ancestors — I can see every moment.
Your arrival... Lovia's end... all threads of a tapestry too vast for me to tell. And yet — how it thrills me.
She trusted me because I heeded her every word. And when the Lady of the{RUBY#[D]Tuonetar} Underworld guided my hand to sever her thread... Even then, she should have rejoiced.
As for you... You'll be leaving this place soon, won't you, Mr. Solovei?
My role here is finished. The believers outside already hail you as their new prophet... and at last, you no longer need to endure the suffering imposed on you.
I still have things I must do. I need to uncover that mad monk's true intentions. For my fallen friend and the people of this land, he must pay for what he has done.
With Lovia's years of secret correspondence with him as evidence, tracing his steps should be much easier. Once again, thank you for your help, Miss Aila.
Ah, so you still don't know a thing... but that's alright. You will soon enough.
I'll take that as an encouragement.
To me, it's already happened. Twice shall that serpent fall — first strangled by the flesh of the faithless, then shrinking away before the light you and I ignite together.
But you shan't be the one to cut off its thread, because that fate does not belong to you.
I don't believe in fate. I'll just do what I can.
Then do what you can. Before the lanterns are lit, I will be here waiting — for you are the hero meant to protect "Elysium."

And you... Forgive me for drawing you here this way. Your thread simply would not catch in the loom of this sublunary sphere, so I had to guide you with those stones. Fitting, for they are just as out of place in this world as you are.
Huh... Huh!? Verna, what's going on? Are you still sure she isn't talking to us!?
W—Well, not anymore! Those stones we saw earlier only fell recently... how could Lady Aila have known about them five hundred years ago...?

By way of apology, I left the last sword forged by the apostle of the golden city using moonlight in the ever-flowing White Spring. After centuries, any bloodstains on its blade should have been washed away.
Please accept this humble gift. Though your fate remains unclear to me, I choose to believe you are the hero of this sublunary sphere — the one destined to fell the undying serpent on our behalf.
This will probably be the last time we meet. If you follow the light and find those who share my bloodline, then you will come to understand my words.
...Are you... talking to someone?
It's nothing. Now, please don't let me keep you any longer, Mr. Solovei. I must begin sealing this place at once.
I hold no resentment toward Lovia. But our children must not be stained by her sins.
That's why the evil and corruption she wrought must be buried... I will seal them all here. This, too, is a part of our preparation for the birth of a god.
We are all tainted by sin... How could we ever hope to behold the moonlight in its purest form?
She vanished...
So... just like back at Thunderclap Reef, it was Lady Aila who guided us to break the sanctum's seal, all so you could retrieve the sword she left behind, {NICKNAME}...
Huh? Come to think of it, Miss Alia said something similar to us back at the Pillar of Embla...
Oh, I see, I see— wait a moment. I don't recognize that name. Who is this Alia?

dialogue.sit:
You briefly explained to Verna about the battle alongside the Ratniki...
"Twice shall that undying serpent rise again, but thrice shall he be struck down..."
"And at last shall he be laid to rest by the heroes of the sublunary sphere..."

dialogue.t: Wow... I'm still not totally sure what just happened, but you've taken down that undying serpent either way, yes?

dialogue.sit: That's right, I am the hero foretold in the prophecy!
Ahem... It was a team effort.

dialogue.t: Heh, I know, right? I knew that even back at Thunderclap Reef! You don't need a prophecy to prove it — you've always been someone I could count on!
But... who is this Alia, anyway? She says she's from five hundred years ago, but I've never seen that name in any records from back then...
Well, whatever! Since Lady Aila brought it up, let's go find that sword!
Ah, you're here. Wait, that will get the altar dirty...
Eek! When the heck did you get in here? We were the ones who opened the seal first... right?

dialogue.sit: Something's off...
Good thing the treasure chests are still here.

So... just like back at Thunderclap Reef, it was Lady Aila who guided us to break the sanctum's seal, all so you could retrieve the sword she left behind, {NICKNAME}...
But Paimon still doesn't get it. Why would Aila give us her sword? And what's this "undying serpent" stuff all about? We're not gonna have to fight some giant snake next, are we?
Anyway, {NICKNAME}, let's retrieve that sword first!
R—Right! If someone as reliable as Lady Aila said it, there must be a reason. Maybe it'll all start to click once we get that sword!
Hmm, this must be the sword Aila was talking about, right?
Yes, yes! This is the sacred blade the first Moonchanter used to offer the very first drop of silver blood to the New Moon — a truly blessed sword of purity!
Ugh, I really want to investigate this place thoroughly... But if we hang around too long, Ehrnrooth, Uncle Krodo, and the others might find the entrance too...
Actually, with all the noise we made just now, there's probably no one on this whole island who hasn't been drawn this way...
Ugh, well... Since we've got the sword and the seal's already broken, I'll just have to find another time to study it properly!
Hmm... this must be the sword Aila was talking about, right? How about it, {NICKNAME}? Did you figure anything out?

dialogue.sit: Not a thing.
Paimon... quick... run... the power in this sword... it's overflowing...!

dialogue.t: Ugh, looks like we really will have to investigate this whole place, huh? But if we hang around too long, Ehrnrooth, Uncle Krodo, and the others might find the entrance too...
Actually, with all the noise we made just now, there's probably no one on this whole island who hasn't been drawn this way...
Ugh, fine, guess we've got no choice... We've got the sword now, and Lady Aila didn't exactly tell us what to do next. Let's get out of here first and figure out the rest later!
Hmm? It's awfully quiet... Ehrnrooth and Uncle Krodo aren't here either. Weren't they hot on our trail?
Maybe all the noise we made earlier got their attention, and they ran off to check somewhere else?
Aha, I get it now! This must be Lady Aila's divine guidance. Even my luck's looking up now that I'm with someone as reliable as you, {NICKNAME}!
Okay, okay, save the celebration for later! You do remember you still owe everybody else an apology for the trouble you caused, right?
Apology? ... Ahem, r—right, yes, of course I do! I'm not the type to get so caught up in reading Lady Aila's records that I forget everything else!
I swear by my mortal name in this sublunary sphere that I'll give everybody a proper and heartfelt apology! It's just... Uh, I'll need to think carefully about how to phrase it first...
Oh! And while we were at work earlier, I came up with a super scientific plan!
Since I have to apologize anyway, why don't we finish checking out the sanctum first before looking for Lady Lauma? That way, we can save time and make my eventual apology more efficient!
A sound plan, I should say.
See? The power of science is— wait, huh!? Aunt Rahetar? When did you get here?
Waaah, you scared us! Umm... We didn't mean to sneak into the Court of the First Edict! It's just... Verna said...
No need to explain. This place may be sealed, but it is not forbidden territory. If outsiders like you were able to enter, then perhaps it was the will of the moonlight.
Exactly! This is all part of the Moon M{RUBY#[D]Kuutar}aiden's sacred guidance! Just like the poems say—
As for you, Vernadska, you're coming with me. The Lady Moonchanter wants to see you — in person.
Huh!? Wait, no, Aunt Rahetar, didn't you just say—
As a priestess, you acted without permission, broke the rules, and tampered with taboos. Aside from outright murder, you've flouted every major law we have.
Now come. Or would you rather the Lady Moonchanter come fetch you herself?
Uhh... {NICKNAME}, Paimon! I'll explain everything later! I swear! But first, I—I'll need—

dialogue.sit: Before Verna can finish her sentence, Rahetar drags her off...

dialogue.t: Well... She sure dug that grave nice and deep for herself, didn't she?
Still, we've got no idea what this Lady Aila wanted us to do. But this sword she left behind...
Uh... If it was meant for us, we might as well hang onto it for now. Looks like a real Frostmoon relic, anyway.

But since we've already taken down the undying serpent, I suppose that means we've fulfilled the task the first Moonchanter entrusted to us, right?

quests.description: You run into Vernadska, the self-proclaimed priestess, again on Hiisi Island. This time, she’s trying to get into a sanctum…
